evidence.honesty: Good: 'fictional vendor's policy library' sits right above the demo, the footer repeats it, and the pilot section says 'we don't have accuracy or time-saved figures'. But the review section aside states 'a draft that arrives already checked gets approved in one pass instead of three', an unsupported quantified saving that contradicts the page's own disclaimer. 'A person replies, usually the same day' under the hero CTA is a service promise the brief does not supply.
evidence.interaction: Step buttons and Replay work by mouse and keyboard (Enter on step 5 moved to the final state), rapid clicks plus Replay and step 4 settled correctly, reduced motion starts on the finished step 5, and the cite chips scroll to the passage and pulse it. But the demo's 'Approve' and 'Send back' buttons have tabindex=-1 (unreachable by keyboard); clicking 'Send back' does nothing and 'Approve' is a no-op, because step 5 auto-approves without the visitor (the 'Your call' step makes the call for you). At 390 the step buttons' accessible names are only '1'..'5' because .step-label is display:none and the visible 'Step n of 5' line is aria-hidden. At 1440, clicking step 5 (button top 249px) puts the 'Approved' result at 999px, below the fold. The status line is not a live region.
evidence.copy: Specific, written microcopy: 'Paperwren left this out rather than guess', 'Gaps are flagged, not filled', 'It won't guess a key rotation period, assume a certification...', pilot steps that name what you keep. Button labels are accurate ('Open a pre-filled email'). The one weak spot is the invented 'one pass instead of three' line.
evidence.first_screen: 1440x900: a specific promise (cite or flag) and a 'Request a pilot' CTA; only the demo heading and the stepper's tab bar peek in at the bottom (panel top y=701), so nothing in view shows an answer being cited. 390x844: H1, lede and CTA fit; no artifact is in view at all (demo panel at y=883).

problems: The demo's reviewer controls are fake: 'Approve'/'Send back' are tabindex=-1, 'Send back' does nothing, and step 5 auto-approves without the visitor, so the 'Your call' moment is not interactive and is unreachable by keyboard.
Unsupported quantified claim 'approved in one pass instead of three' (review section aside), contradicting the brief and the page's own 'no time-saved figures' line.
Accessibility gaps: 12 AA contrast failures (muted #7a818c text), mobile step buttons named only '1'-'5', the check marks hidden on mobile, and the demo below the first screen at both widths.

The speed comes from fewer rounds, not from skipping the review.' This is a quantified time/effort saving (three review rounds reduced to one) presented as fact. The brief says 'no accuracy or time-saved numbers', and the page itself later says it has no time-saved figures.
hard_fail_flags.steps: Open packets/P013/A/index.html from disk at 1440x900, scroll to the section headed 'Written for the person who has to approve it', and read the yellow-ruled paragraph below the three columns (index.html line 155).

evidence.clarity: The H1 'Security questionnaires drafted from your own policies. Every answer cited or flagged.' names the job and the guarantee. The lede adds who (vendors answering enterprise buyers) and the approval step. CTA 'Request a pilot by email' plus 'Opens a blank email to pilots@paperwren.example. Nothing to upload, no call to book.' says exactly what happens next.
evidence.fit: Both audiences get a real path: a four-step handoff ('Owner: Sales engineer / Paperwren / Security lead / Sales engineer') plus separate 'If you're the sales engineer' and 'If you're the security lead' columns. The demo shows one cited answer and one flagged question with no upload. Every mailto points to pilots@paperwren.example. Partners are unnamed, and the 'Accuracy' and 'Time saved' facts both read 'Not measured yet'.
evidence.distinctiveness: The page applies its own product logic to itself: superscript citations on claims linking to a 'Notes on this page' section ('Every claim above carries a note or a flag, the way an answer should'), Cited/Flagged chips reused in the pilot facts, and an agent log in mono type. The layout is still a familiar split hero, then numbered steps, then two columns.
evidence.proof: 1440: the sample card sits in the hero (top y=124) with the question, agent log, cited draft '[1]'/'[2]' and the source quotes with section numbers. The second tab, 'Q 9.1 Penetration test (Flagged)', shows 'No source in your policies, so nothing was drafted' with the closest miss quoted, which answers the 'makes things up' doubt directly. It is labelled 'Illustrative: a made-up questionnaire and made-up policies' at the top of the card. Counts are consistent (2 passages, 2 citations, 14 documents/212 sections in both tabs).
evidence.craft: axe: 0 violations (probe and my own run including best-practice). Tokens on :root for colour, type scale (--h1/--h2 clamp), spacing and section rhythm; inline CSS is ordered by section; no external fonts. Defects: the footnote markers render at 8.84-11.56px with 10x11 to 13x15px hit areas, and the 'Owner' labels are 11px. Replay sets card.style.minHeight while hiding content, which leaves a blank card body during the replay. 39 KB HTML plus a 66 KB og.png, which is only referenced by an absolute URL.
evidence.mobile: 390: no overflow (0px at 390 and 320 in probe and my test); the nav wraps to a visible second row of 44px links (no hidden menu needed); the hero CTA is full-width at 52px; tabs stack as full-width 48px rows; the Approve/Send back buttons are 152x48. However the sample card starts at y=768, so the artifact is below the first screen. Tapping 'Replay the draft' at 390 (button at y=402) moved the button to y=-622 and left the viewport showing an empty white card while the steps rebuilt about 1000px above (screenshot B-390-replay-300ms). The footnote links are tiny tap targets.
evidence.honesty: Labels appear where the material is: 'Illustrative: a made-up questionnaire and made-up policies. Nothing here is uploaded or sent.' sits at the top of the card, and the reviewer is shown as 'Priya Natarajan · Security lead (sample)'. The pilot facts list 'Accuracy: Not measured yet', 'Time saved: Not measured yet', 'No public pricing yet', and the CTA states what the click does before you commit. A minor stretch: note 5's 'Sales engineers tell us the draft changes their work from chasing answers to reviewing them' is an unattributed anecdote, though it contains no number.
evidence.interaction: Operated at 1440 and 390: Approve gives 'Approved ... locked to this questionnaire', moves focus to 'Reset the sample', and Enter on Reset restores 'Awaiting approval' with focus back on Approve. Send back, Write the answer and Mark not applicable each give their own outcome. The status is a role=status live region. Tabs use roving tabindex, ArrowLeft/Right switch panels, state is kept per tab, and switching tab mid-replay cancels the replay cleanly. No console errors. Problems: pressing Enter on 'Replay the draft' disables the focused button, so document.activeElement becomes BODY and the next Tab jumps to the first footnote near the top of the page. Home/End are not handled on the tablist. Under reduced motion the replay still steps in over about 3s, without transitions, and everything returns.
evidence.copy: Specific nouns from the buyer's world ('Q 9.1 Penetration test', 'Vulnerability Management Policy §5, which covers internal scanning only', 'Mark not applicable'), exact button labels ('Request a pilot by email', 'Reset the sample'), and plain disclaimers ('We will not print a number we have not measured'). 'Not for you yet if your policies live in people's heads' answers a real objection. Slightly long overall (6.5k characters of body text).
evidence.first_screen: 1440x900: the promise, the CTA with its stated outcome, and the cited sample answer with its log and sources all sit in one viewport. 390x844: the promise, the full-width CTA and 'Opens a blank email to pilots@paperwren.example' are visible, but only the card's title line ('Sample questionnaire · Northwind Logistics') peeks in at the bottom, so nothing in view yet makes the promise believable on the phone.

problems: Replay drops keyboard focus to <body> (the focused button disables itself), and at 390 the rebuild happens off-screen above the tapped button, leaving an empty card in view.
Footnote superscript links are 8.84-11.56px text with 10x11 to 13x15px tap targets, and the 'Owner' labels are 11px.
At 390 the sample card starts at y=768, so the artifact is below the first screen on the phone.

reason: B's artifact is genuinely operable by mouse and keyboard: an ARIA tablist with arrow keys, four reviewer outcomes with a reset path, focus management and a live status. It passes axe with zero violations, keeps every number honest with labels at the point of use, and shows the cited and the flagged case in the first screen at 1440. A's stepper works, but its reviewer buttons are decorative and unreachable by keyboard, it has 12 contrast failures, and it carries an unsupported 'one pass instead of three' claim. Only evidence that B's replay or footnote issues break real use on a common device would change my mind, and they do not.
